```{r Step 0: Pull in ANES Data, include=TRUE}
anes_panel <- read_dta(here("00_rawdata", "ANES_Data", "anes_timeseries_cdf_stata_20260205.dta"))
```

```{r Step 1: Cleaning Up the Dataset, include=TRUE}
# Check the variables
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(year = VCF0004, trust_gov_index = VCF0656, trust_gov = VCF0604, econ_views = VCF0870, stock_owns = VCF9224, social_class = VCF0149, person_finances = VCF0880, person_finances_scale = VCF0880a, personal_finances_next = VCF0881, age = VCF0101, age_group = VCF0102, gender = VCF0104, race = VCF0105a, educ = VCF0110, income_group = VCF0114, emp_status = VCF0116, homeowner = VCF0146, marital_stat = VCF0147, partisan_id = VCF0301, partisan_strength = VCF0305, pol_interest = VCF0310, union_mem = VCF0127)


#Initial Diagnostics
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    personal_finances_change = case_when(
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% 1:5 ~ as.numeric(person_finances_scale),
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    personal_finances_scale_factor = factor(
      personal_finances_change,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "Much better",
        "Somewhat better",
        "Same",
        "Somewhat worse",
        "Much worse"
      )
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    personal_finances_scale_clean = case_when(
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% 1:5 ~
        as.numeric(person_finances_scale),
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% c(8, 9) ~
        NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    personal_finance_direction = case_when(
      personal_finances_scale_clean %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Better",
      personal_finances_scale_clean == 3 ~ "Same",
      personal_finances_scale_clean %in% c(4, 5) ~ "Worse",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    personal_finance_direction = factor(
      personal_finance_direction,
      levels = c("Better", "Same", "Worse")
    )
  )
#Recoding Variables (Brought Over from Part 1)
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    trust_gov_index = na_if(trust_gov_index, 999)
  )

#Same Thing for Economic Views
anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2024) %>%
  count(econ_views, sort = TRUE)

#Recode Data to Only show valid entries
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    trust_gov_index = na_if(trust_gov_index, 999),
    econ_views = case_when(
      econ_views %in% c(1, 3, 5) ~ econ_views,
      econ_views %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    # Trust
    trust_gov_index = if_else(
      trust_gov_index == 999,
      NA_real_,
      as.numeric(trust_gov_index)
    ),

    # Economic views
    econ_views = case_when(
      as.numeric(econ_views) %in% c(1, 3, 5) ~ as.numeric(econ_views),
      as.numeric(econ_views) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Stock ownership
    stock_owns = case_when(
      as.numeric(stock_owns) == 1 ~ 1,
      as.numeric(stock_owns) == 2 ~ 0,
      as.numeric(stock_owns) %in% c(-8, -9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Homeownership
    homeowner = case_when(
      as.numeric(homeowner) == 1 ~ 1,
      as.numeric(homeowner) == 2 ~ 0,
      as.numeric(homeowner) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Income percentile group
    income_group = as.numeric(income_group)
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    econ_views_factor = factor(
      econ_views,
      levels = c(1, 3, 5),
      labels = c(
        "Get better",
        "Stay about the same",
        "Get worse"
      )
    ),

    income_group_factor = factor(
      income_group,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "0–16th percentile",
        "17–33rd percentile",
        "34–67th percentile",
        "68–95th percentile",
        "96–100th percentile"
      )
    )
  )

#Adding in new variable - external efficacy index
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(
    efficacy_index = VCF0648
  )

summary(anes_panel$efficacy_index)

table(

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    efficacy_index = case_when(
      as.numeric(efficacy_index) %in% 1:100 ~ as.numeric(efficacy_index),
      as.numeric(efficacy_index) >100 ~ NA_real_,

  ) 

anes_panel %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(efficacy_index)),

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(
    government_care = VCF0609

    government_care = case_when(

    ),
    government_care_factor = factor(
      government_care,
      levels = 1:3,
      labels = c(
        "Agree",
        "Disagree",
        "Neither"
      )
    )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(
    government_say = VCF0613
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    government_say = case_when(
      as.numeric(government_say) %in% 1:3 ~ as.numeric(government_say),
      as.numeric(government_say) == 9 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    government_say_factor = factor(
      government_say,
      levels = 1:3,
      labels = c(
        "Agree",
        "Disagree",
        "Neither"
      )
    )
  )

table(
  anes_panel$government_say,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

#Turn Dataset into Survey Object
anes_svy <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000) %>%
  as_survey_design(
    ids = 1,
    weights = VCF0009z
  ) 

anes_svy

anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2024) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(government_care)),
    agree = sum(government_care == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    disagree = sum(government_care == 2, na.rm = TRUE),

anes_panel %>%
```

```{r Step 2: Model Relationship between Income and External Efficacy, include=TRUE}
#First Model on If People Think the Government Cares what they Have to Say
government_care_income <- lapply(
  sort(unique(anes_panel$year[
    anes_panel$year >= 2000 & anes_panel$year <= 2024
  ])),
  function(y) {

    data_y <- anes_panel %>%
      filter(
        year == y,
        !is.na(government_care),
        !is.na(income_group_factor),
        !is.na(VCF0009z)
      )

    if (nrow(data_y) == 0) return(NULL)

    design_y <- survey::svydesign(
      ids = ~1,
      weights = ~VCF0009z,
      data = data_y
    )

    # Recode agreement as binary
    data_y <- data_y %>%
      mutate(government_care_agree = as.numeric(government_care == 1))

    design_y <- survey::svydesign(
      ids = ~1,
      weights = ~VCF0009z,
      data = data_y
    )

    means <- survey::svyby(
      ~government_care_agree,
      ~income_group_factor,
      design_y,
      survey::svymean,
      vartype = c("se", "ci")
    )

    means %>%
      mutate(year = y)
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()

government_care_income

#Second Model on If they Think they Have a Say in What the Government Does
government_say_income <- lapply(
  sort(unique(anes_panel$year[
    anes_panel$year >= 2000 & anes_panel$year <= 2024
  ])),
  function(y) {

    data_y <- anes_panel %>%
      filter(
        year == y,
        !is.na(government_say),
        !is.na(income_group_factor),
        !is.na(VCF0009z)
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        government_say_agree = as.numeric(government_say == 1)
      )

    if (nrow(data_y) == 0) return(NULL)

    design_y <- survey::svydesign(
      ids = ~1,
      weights = ~VCF0009z,
      data = data_y
    )

    means <- survey::svyby(
      ~government_say_agree,
      ~income_group_factor,
      design_y,
      survey::svymean,
      vartype = c("se", "ci")
    )

    means %>%
      mutate(year = y)
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()

government_say_income

#Putting the Two Models in Side-by-Side Comparison
care_gradient <- government_care_income %>%
  filter(
    income_group_factor %in% c(
      "0–16th percentile",
      "96–100th percentile"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(year, income_group_factor, government_care_agree) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = income_group_factor,
    values_from = government_care_agree
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    care_gradient =
      `96–100th percentile` -
      `0–16th percentile`
  ) %>%
  select(year, care_gradient)

say_gradient <- government_say_income %>%
  filter(
    income_group_factor %in% c(
      "0–16th percentile",
      "96–100th percentile"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(year, income_group_factor, government_say_agree) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = income_group_factor,
    values_from = government_say_agree
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    say_gradient =
      `96–100th percentile` -
      `0–16th percentile`
  ) %>%
  select(year, say_gradient)

efficacy_income_gradients <- care_gradient %>%
  left_join(say_gradient, by = "year")

efficacy_income_gradients
```

```{r Step 3: Running Regression Models for Each Efficacy Outcome to see Income's Effect, include=TRUE}
government_care_income_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_care),
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    government_care_agree = as.numeric(government_care == 1)
  )

design_care_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = government_care_income_time
)

model_care_income_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_care_agree ~
    income_group_factor * factor(year),
  design = design_care_time,
  family = quasibinomial()
)

care_predictions <- predictions(
  model_care_income_time,
  newdata = datagrid(
    income_group_factor = levels(anes_panel$income_group_factor),
    year = c(
      "2000", "2004", "2008",
      "2012", "2016", "2020", "2024"
    )
  ),
  type = "response"
)

care_predictions

government_say_income_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_say),
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    government_say_agree = as.numeric(government_say == 1)
  )

design_say_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = government_say_income_time
)

model_say_income_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_say_agree ~
    income_group_factor * factor(year),
  design = design_say_time,
  family = quasibinomial()
)

say_predictions <- ggpredict(
  model_say_income_time,
  terms = c("income_group_factor", "year")
)

care_predictions <- ggpredict(
  model_care_income_time,
  terms = c("income_group_factor", "year")
)

say_predictions
care_predictions
```

```{r Step 4: Joint Wald Tests for Both Outcomes, include=TRUE}
# Identify the income × year interaction coefficients
interaction_idx_care <- grep(
  "income_group_factor",
  names(coef(model_care_income_time))
)

interaction_idx_care <- interaction_idx_care[
  grepl(
    "factor\\(year\\)",
    names(coef(model_care_income_time))[interaction_idx_care]
  )
]

# Extract coefficients and covariance matrix
beta_care <- coef(model_care_income_time)[interaction_idx_care]

V_care <- vcov(model_care_income_time)[
  interaction_idx_care,
  interaction_idx_care,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Wald statistic
W_care <- as.numeric(
  t(beta_care) %*%
    solve(V_care) %*%
    beta_care
)

# Convert to F statistic
q_care <- length(beta_care)

F_care <- W_care / q_care

df_care <- model_care_income_time$df.residual

p_care <- pf(
  F_care,
  df1 = q_care,
  df2 = df_care,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  F = F_care,
  df1 = q_care,
  df2 = df_care,
  p_value = p_care
)

# Identify the income × year interaction coefficients
interaction_idx_say <- grep(
  "income_group_factor",
  names(coef(model_say_income_time))
)

interaction_idx_say <- interaction_idx_say[
  grepl(
    "factor\\(year\\)",
    names(coef(model_say_income_time))[interaction_idx_say]
  )
]

# Extract coefficients and covariance matrix
beta_say <- coef(model_say_income_time)[interaction_idx_say]

V_say <- vcov(model_say_income_time)[
  interaction_idx_say,
  interaction_idx_say,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Wald statistic
W_say <- as.numeric(
  t(beta_say) %*%
    solve(V_say) %*%
    beta_say
)

# Convert to F statistic
q_say <- length(beta_say)

F_say <- W_say / q_say

df_say <- model_say_income_time$df.residual

p_say <- pf(
  F_say,
  df1 = q_say,
  df2 = df_say,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  F = F_say,
  df1 = q_say,
  df2 = df_say,
  p_value = p_say
)

efficacy_interaction_tests <- data.frame(
  outcome = c(
    "Officials care what people like me think",
    "People like me have a say in government"
  ),
  F = c(F_care, F_say),
  df1 = c(q_care, q_say),
  df2 = c(df_care, df_say),
  p_value = c(p_care, p_say)
)

efficacy_interaction_tests

#although the predicted probabilities show a substantial descriptive reduction in the income gradient—from roughly 28 percentage points in 2000 to 5 points in 2024—we don't have strong enough statistical evidence to conclude that the income profile itself changed across the survey years. However, there is evidence that the relationship between income and perceived political voice differs across years.
```

```{r Step 5: Test on Income Gradients over time for both measures, include=TRUE}
care_gradients <- comparisons(
  model_care_income_time,
  variables = list(
    income_group_factor = c(
      "0–16th percentile",
      "96–100th percentile"
    )
  ),
  by = "year",
  type = "response"
)

say_gradients <- comparisons(
  model_say_income_time,
  variables = list(
    income_group_factor = c(
      "0–16th percentile",
      "96–100th percentile"
    )
  ),
  by = "year",
  type = "response"
)

care_gradient_table <- care_gradients %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  )

say_gradient_table <- say_gradients %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  )

care_gradient_table
say_gradient_table

efficacy_gradient_table <- care_gradient_table %>%
  rename(
    care_gradient = estimate,
    care_low = conf.low,
    care_high = conf.high,
    care_p = p.value
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    say_gradient_table %>%
      rename(
        say_gradient = estimate,
        say_low = conf.low,
        say_high = conf.high,
        say_p = p.value
      ),
    by = "year"
  )

efficacy_gradient_table

#Plotting the Results
# Prepare care gradients
care_gradient_plot <- as.data.frame(care_gradients) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = "Officials care what people like me think"
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    outcome
  )

# Prepare say gradients
say_gradient_plot <- as.data.frame(say_gradients) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = "People like me have a say in government"
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    outcome
  )

# Combine
efficacy_gradient_plot <- bind_rows(
  care_gradient_plot,
  say_gradient_plot
) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(as.character(year))
  )

# Plot
efficacy_gradient_plot_save <- ggplot(
  efficacy_gradient_plot,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = estimate,
    color = outcome,
    fill = outcome
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = conf.low,
      ymax = conf.high
    ),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Income gradient in perceived political efficacy",
    color = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    title = "Income differences in perceived political efficacy have narrowed",
    subtitle = "Highest-income group minus lowest-income group; 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  here("05_images", "Efficacy_GradientPlot.jpg"),
  plot = efficacy_gradient_plot_save
)
```
